stem.en: I was just about ___ when the phone rang.

why.en: Be about to + verb means something was going to happen very soon: about to leave.
why.uz: Be about to + feʼl biror narsa juda tez sodir boʻlishi kutilganini bildiradi: about to leave.
why.ru: Be about to + глагол — что-то вот-вот должно было произойти: about to leave.

stem.en: The meeting ___ at ten, but it was cancelled at the last minute.

why.en: Was to have + past participle describes a plan in the past that did not happen.
why.uz: Was to have + uchinchi shakl oʻtmishda rejalashtirilgan, lekin amalga oshmagan ishni bildiradi.
why.ru: Was to have + третья форма — план в прошлом, который не осуществился.

stem.en: She knew that one day she ___ a doctor.

why.en: The future seen from a past moment (she knew) uses would + the base verb: would become.
why.uz: Oʻtmishdagi paytdan (she knew) qaralgan kelajak would + asosiy shakl bilan: would become.
why.ru: Будущее с точки зрения прошлого (she knew): would + начальная форма: would become.

stem.en: We were going to ___ you, but we lost your number.

why.en: Was/were going to + the base verb describes a past intention: were going to call.
why.uz: Was/were going to + asosiy shakl oʻtmishdagi niyatni bildiradi: were going to call.
why.ru: Was/were going to + начальная форма — намерение в прошлом: were going to call.

stem.en: Every student in both classes ___ to bring a calculator.

why.en: Every + singular noun takes a singular verb: every student needs.
why.uz: Every + birlikdagi ot birlikdagi feʼl bilan keladi: every student needs.
why.ru: Every + существительное в единственном числе требует глагола в единственном: every student needs.

stem.en: The number of students ___ increased this year.

why.en: The subject is the number (one figure), so the verb is singular: has increased.
why.uz: Ega — the number (bitta raqam), shuning uchun feʼl birlikda: has increased.
why.ru: Подлежащее — the number (одно число), поэтому глагол в единственном числе: has increased.

stem.en: A number of problems ___ been reported since the update.

why.en: A number of + plural noun means several, so the verb is plural: have been reported.
why.uz: A number of + koʻplikdagi ot «bir nechta» degani, shuning uchun feʼl koʻplikda: have been reported.
why.ru: A number of + существительное во множественном = «несколько», глагол во множественном: have been reported.

stem.en: Ten kilometres ___ a long way to walk in this heat.

why.en: A distance seen as one amount takes a singular verb: ten kilometres is a long way.
why.uz: Bitta miqdor sifatida qaralgan masofa birlikdagi feʼl oladi: ten kilometres is a long way.
why.ru: Расстояние как единое количество требует глагола в единственном числе: ten kilometres is.

why.uz: Whereby (= by which) tizim qanday usulda ishlashini bildiruvchi gapni kiritadi.
why.ru: Whereby (= by which) вводит способ, по которому работает система.

stem.en: The castle, the walls ___ are over five metres thick, is open to visitors.

why.en: For things, noun + of which shows possession: the walls of which (= whose walls).
why.uz: Narsalar uchun ot + of which egalikni bildiradi: the walls of which (= whose walls).
why.ru: Для предметов существительное + of which выражает принадлежность: the walls of which (= whose walls).

stem.en: He failed the test, ___ point he decided to change his study method.

why.en: At which point refers back to the moment just described: at that point.
why.uz: At which point hozirgina aytilgan paytga qaytib ishora qiladi: oʻsha paytda.
why.ru: At which point отсылает к только что описанному моменту: в тот момент.

stem.en: There were forty applicants, the majority of ___ were from abroad.

why.en: After a preposition (of), people are referred to with whom; them would need a new sentence.
why.uz: Predlogdan (of) keyin odamlarga whom orqali ishora qilinadi; them uchun yangi gap kerak boʻlardi.
why.ru: После предлога (of) о людях говорят whom; с them потребовалось бы новое предложение.

stem.en: Are you coming to the party? — I hope ___.

why.en: So replaces a whole positive clause after hope: I hope so (= I hope I am coming).
why.uz: Hope dan keyin so butun tasdiq gapning oʻrnini bosadi: I hope so (= I hope I am coming).
why.ru: После hope слово so заменяет целое утвердительное предложение: I hope so.

stem.en: She said she would finish the report today, and she ___.

why.en: The auxiliary did stands for the whole past action: and she did (= she finished it).
why.uz: Did yordamchi feʼli butun oʻtgan harakat oʻrnini bosadi: and she did (= she finished it).
why.ru: Вспомогательный did заменяет всё прошедшее действие: and she did (= she finished it).

stem.en: Will the shop be open on Sunday? — I'm afraid ___.

why.en: Not replaces a negative clause after I'm afraid: I'm afraid not (= it won't be open).
why.uz: I'm afraid dan keyin not butun inkor gapning oʻrnini bosadi: I'm afraid not.
why.ru: После I'm afraid слово not заменяет отрицательное предложение: I'm afraid not.

stem.en: My brother can play the guitar, and ___ my sister.

why.en: To agree with a positive sentence, use so + the same auxiliary + subject: so can my sister.
why.uz: Tasdiq gapga qoʻshilish uchun so + oʻsha yordamchi feʼl + ega: so can my sister.
why.ru: Чтобы присоединиться к утверждению: so + тот же вспомогательный глагол + подлежащее: so can my sister.
